articles.title: USL and players ratify new CBAs, raising salaries and introducing 12-month deals
articles.summary: New pacts include CBA for first-division USL Premier. Base pay for Championship grows from $31k to $42k. Agreements run through the 2030 season. The United Soccer League and USL Players Association announced the ratification of new collective bargaining agreements for two levels of the…
body: Among the headline items of the deals is the introduction of 12-month contracts for players, a codified first in the US lower divisions. The first USL CBAs worked to standardize 10-month contracts; before then, clubs varied in their commitments to players. Championship players will earn a base compensation (which includes housing) of $42,000 in 2026 – up from $31,000 – with that floor increasing annually over the term of the agreement. The USL Premier will also launch with 12-month contracts and a compensation floor of $67,500 in 2028 with annual increases worked into the CBA.

“This collective bargaining agreement is a significant step forward for the USL and our players and reflects the shared commitment on both sides to continue growing the game and advancing professional standards,” USL president and CEO Paul McDonough said in a statement. “It provides long-term stability for our players, clubs and leagues, and greater confidence to invest in the future of the USL.”

articles.title: Moyes reveals he has never spoken to Everton owner but is defiant after transfer blows
articles.summary: Friedkin Group under scrutiny after summer of sales. Moyes hopes for ‘something special’ with weaker squad. David Moyes has not spoken to the Everton owner and chair, Dan Friedkin, in the 20 months since he returned to the club as manager.
body: Moyes exposed an astonishing disconnect at the club when confirming he has had no contact with Friedkin, founder and chief executive of The Friedkin Group, since replacing Sean Dyche as manager in January 2025. TFG president, Marc Watts, is Everton’s executive chair and Rishi Majithia, Friedkin’s son-in-law, is the owner’s day-to-day representative at the club. But with TFG’s ambition for Everton under scrutiny after the transfer window, and amid claims they are looking for fresh investment or even to sell the club, Moyes’s revelation raises further questions over the company’s commitment.

The Everton manager admitted any successful club “needs to be aligned” at the top and added: “We’ve got new owners in who are still feeling their way in the club. I think if we get to know each other more it will get better.” Moyes, whose main point of contact at Everton is the chief executive, Angus Kinnear, was later asked whether he had ever had a conversation with Dan Friedkin. “Er, no,” he replied. So you’ve never met him? “No,” said Moyes.

articles.title: Greaves makes more history with win at Czech Darts Open
articles.summary: Beau Greaves made more darting history as she became the first woman to win a match on the PDC's European Tour - a feat that secured her a second-round clash with Luke Humphries at the Czech Darts Open.
body: The 22-year-old rallied from 3-1 down to beat Daryl Gurney 6-4 in Prague on Friday night and will now play world No 2 Humphries in the last-32 on Saturday evening, with the winner meeting Nathan Aspinall or Andrew Gilding in round three on Sunday.

Greaves' latest landmark moment follows becoming the first woman to hit a nine-darter on the PDC Pro Tour, against Mensur Suljovic back in February, and the first to win a PDC ranking title, doing so when she edged Michael Smith 8-7 at Players Championship 11.
She was also the first woman to qualify for a European Tour event when she reached last month's Hungarian Darts Trophy.

Greaves lost to Rob Cross in the first round in Budapest but her run in Prague will now last at least one more match after defeating Gurney, a player she had suffered a narrow 3-2 loss to in round one of the 2026 World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace.

articles.title: How influencers at US Open are testing boundaries of tennis etiquette
articles.summary: A huge discussion around tennis etiquette has been sparked at the US Open due to the disruption caused by a growing number of content creators and influencers at Flushing Meadows.
body: The number of content creators who have been accredited to cover this year's final Grand Slam of the year has doubled from last year in a move by organisers to reach new audiences. Yet the noise and disturbance caused by them in the stands as been felt by players on court.

Chair umpire Kader Nouni admonished a group of influencers in a suite for recording a video in the middle of a point, while another incident saw a creator using the use of a bright portable ring light to take photos.
Meanwhile, in Naomi Osaka's second-round victory, chair umpire Marijana Veljovic asked fans several times to be quiet.

Some players have questioned whether the push for online engagement has gone too far with two-time champion Osaka saying: "I think obviously if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport.".
